props.title: AI Engineering Skills Map: Using coding agents
props.thesis: Ng's third map is about steering coding agents, and he is blunt that longer unattended runs are not the goal.
props.take: Set verifiable goals, keep the context current, and intervene by risk — not by vibe.

phases.label: Plan
phases.line: Research, explore the codebase, then write a spec and an execution plan

phases.label: Execute
phases.line: Build and verify together, in steps whose results you can check

phases.label: Operate
phases.line: Release gates, log inspection, and a route back to earlier phases

phases.label: Calibrate autonomy
phases.line: Collaborate, delegate, or let it retry — decide by risk and cost

phases.label: Verify the verifier
phases.line: Automated checks stop agents, but their criteria need scrutiny too

phases.label: Hold the context
phases.line: AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, hooks, retrospectives, clearing agent debt

narration: The third map is the one most people need, and it ends on a warning. [pause] Ng's process has three phases. Plan. Execute. Operate. Planning means research, codebase exploration, and a specification covering requirements, design and architecture. Execution pairs building with testing. Operating adds release gates and log inspection. And a failed check sends you back a phase. [pause] How much planning? That depends. A throwaway prototype needs a sentence. An established product serving real users deserves a checked specification. [pause] Then calibrate autonomy. Work alongside the agent, delegate a chunk, or let it retry toward a clear goal. Decide by risk and cost, not by habit. [pause] Then verify the verifier. Automated checks tell an agent when to stop. But the criteria themselves need scrutiny, and sometimes a human still has to look. [pause] Then hold the context. An agents file records architecture and conventions. Hooks trigger reviews. Retrospectives capture lessons. And you clear the debt the agents generate. [pause] Ng names the warning signs too. Overengineering. Missing verification. Stopping too early. And destructive actions. [pause] He also says to learn how the harness itself works. How it retrieves code, how it manages the context window, how it spawns subagents. [pause] His closing warning is direct. Social media exaggerates how useful those hours-long, million-token runs really are.
